units.text: Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java is a free, open-source library for creating, reading, and manipulating PDF documents in Java applications. It enables developers to generate PDFs from scratch, extract text and images, fill interactive form fields, and manage annotations and form controls such as radio buttons without requiring external dependencies. Built for Java 11 and later, it supports common workflows like converting content to PDF, inspecting document structure, and exporting resources. Users include Java developers building reporting tools, form processors, and document automation systems who need a lightweight, permissively licensed PDF solution.

Create and modify PDF documents by adding pages and text fragments, then saving the result to a file, as demonstrated by instantiating a Document, adding a Page, inserting a TextFragment, and calling save.
Extract text using TextAbsorber to traverse pages and retrieve content, and extract images by iterating XImage objects from page resources and saving them to streams.
Work with form fields by accessing the Form object, setting values on specific fields like TextBoxField, and iterating all fields to read or modify their names and values.
Manage annotations by creating WidgetAnnotation instances with a Rectangle, then configuring their border and background colors through the characteristics object.
Build and inspect table content by adding TextFragment and RadioButtonOptionField objects to a Cell, then querying the cell's paragraphs collection to verify its contents.
Configure annotation borders by creating a Border object for a RadioButtonOptionField, setting its style to Dashed, and reading the border properties back.
Create a page-level widget annotation and set its border color, then read it back.
The following workflows demonstrate common tasks with Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java, including adding form fields, extracting content, and manipulating annotations.
Insert a text fragment and radio button option into a table cell.
Extract all text from a PDF using TextAbsorber.
Save all images from a specific page as PNG files.
Create a new PDF with a single text fragment.
Populate form fields and iterate over all form fields.
Set and retrieve the background color of a widget annotation.
Configure and inspect the border style of a radio button option.
Add multiple radio button options to a cell in insertion order.

The entry point for working with PDF documents is the Document class, which exposes page collections and convenience operations through facades such as PdfFileEditor and PdfContentEditor. This module, org.aspose:aspose-pdf-foss version 26.8.0, targets Java 11 and implements ISO 32000-1:2008.
The top-level package org groups the Aspose PDF FOSS for Java module under the org.aspose namespace.
The org.aspose package organizes the public API surface for Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java, grouping types under the org.aspose.pdf subpackage.
The org.aspose.pdf package contains the core Document class, page collections, and facades such as PdfFileEditor and PdfContentEditor that provide document-level operations.
The getting started guide introduces core concepts and walks through initial setup and basic usage of Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java.
The how-to guides and FAQ provide practical examples and answers to common questions for working with PDF documents using Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java.
The full API reference documents all public classes, methods, and functionality available in the org.aspose:aspose-pdf-foss package version 26.8.0.

Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java provides a Java library for creating, reading, and manipulating PDF documents, targeting developers who need a free, open-source subset of Aspose.PDF for Java functionality, with version 26.8.0 requiring Java 11 or higher.
Out of scope for this edition are OCR of scanned images, conversion to or from non-PDF formats beyond HTML/XML, full XFA form rendering, and 3D annotations or PRC/U3D streams.
A single Document instance is not thread-safe, so developers must use one Document per thread when processing documents in parallel.

Partial implementation includes unsupported PdfFileSecurity.setAllowExceptions, limited text replacement for non-Latin scripts, constrained resource optimization, partial tagged PDF structure tree coverage, PDF/X validation and conversion without dedicated test coverage, and public-key-encrypted PDF support without out-of-the-box helpers.

Build and test Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java using the CI workflows in .github/workflows/ and documentation in docs/; the library targets Java 11 and is published as org.aspose:aspose-pdf-foss version 26.8.0.

Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java provides a free, open-source subset of functionality for PDF processing in Java applications, while the commercial Aspose.PDF for Java product extends this with additional features, advanced capabilities, and enterprise support.
